name: Mitochondrial Disorder Due to a Defect in Assembly or Maturation of the Respiratory Chain Complexes

criteria.description: Deficient activity of one or more respiratory chain complexes in muscle or fibroblasts
Identification of pathogenic variants in nuclear genes involved in assembly or maturation of respiratory chain complexes
Presence of multisystemic clinical manifestations consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX)-negative fibers

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Deficient respiratory chain complex activity plus genetic confirmation of pathogenic variants in assembly or maturation genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by clinical features and muscle biopsy findings but requires biochemical and genetic confirmation.

searchTerms: muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
abnormal muscle fibers with red staining

pathognomonic.notes: Elevated serum lactate due to impaired oxidative phosphorylation

common.notes: Frequently reported symptom due to impaired energy metabolism
searchTerms: muscle weakness and poor exercise tolerance

common.notes: Impaired coordination due to cerebellar involvement

occasional.notes: Occur in some patients with CNS involvement

laboratory: Elevated serum and CSF lactate and pyruvate
Abnormal respiratory chain enzyme activities in muscle or fibroblasts
Elevated creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing basal ganglia lesions or stroke-like lesions
Muscle MRI demonstrating fatty infiltration and atrophy
genetic: Pathogenic variants in nuclear genes encoding assembly factors for complexes I, III, IV, or V
Mitochondrial DNA depletion or multiple deletions secondary to nuclear gene defects
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Primary mitochondrial DNA depletion without nuclear assembly gene defects
Earlier onset with severe multisystem involvement
Predominant optic neuropathy without multisystem involvement
Mitochondrial DNA point mutations rather than nuclear gene defects

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia in a young patient
Unexplained lactic acidosis with multisystem involvement
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers with deficient respiratory chain activity
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
Parikh S, Goldstein A, Karaa A, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015 Sep;17(9):689-701.
